registration_timing: Before creation of the Python WLE scoring core and TAM parity fixtures.
purpose: Evaluate Warm weighted-likelihood Person scoring as an explicitly separate fixed-calibration estimator for boundary and interior response patterns.

theory.reference: Warm, T. A. (1989). Weighted likelihood estimation of ability in item response theory. Psychometrika, 54, 427-450. https://doi.org/10.1007/BF02294627
theory.polytomous_reference: Magis, D. (2015). A note on weighted likelihood and Jeffreys modal estimation of proficiency levels in polytomous item response models. Psychometrika, 80, 200-204. https://doi.org/10.1007/s11336-013-9378-5
theory.fixed_calibration_logit: log P(Y_r=k | theta) = intercept[r,k] + slope[r,k] * theta - log_normalizer

python_core_contract.missing_rows: Omitted independently by Person through an observed-row mask.
python_core_contract.row_weights: Finite positive weights enter the score, information, and information derivative; non-positive or non-finite retained weights fail closed.
python_core_contract.boundary_rule: WLE may return a finite adjusted-score root for all-minimum/all-maximum patterns, but the result must never be labelled a finite JMLE MLE.
python_core_contract.root_method: Bracketed Brent root on the unrounded adjusted score with symmetric bracket expansion.
python_core_contract.no_root_action: Return an explicit unavailable status; never clamp and report a boundary as converged.

validation_matrix.binary_closed_form: For n equal Rasch items and raw score x, theta_WLE must equal logit((x+0.5)/(n+1)), including x=0 and x=n.
validation_matrix.weighted_duplication: Integer row weights must equal literal row duplication within 1e-10.
validation_matrix.derivative_check: The analytical I_prime must match a centered finite difference of I within 1e-6 and U_W must match the derivative of log-likelihood + 0.5 log I within 1e-6.
